< Little RPG

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 9 August 2026

The short version

Little RPG runs on your device. Your save lives in your own device's storage and is never uploaded: we cannot see it, and we cannot recover it.

One feature does leave your device, and you should know about it before you play: the leaderboard. When you rebirth or awaken, the game sends a short line to a database so the boards can rank you: a random id for your device, the nickname you chose, your league, your deepest stage and your best weekly sprint. No name, no email, no account, no location, nothing about your phone. That is the whole of it, and the section The leaderboard below spells out every field, when each one is sent, and how to have your row deleted.

The game is free. If a version of it sells gems, the payment is handled by the app store and never by us. See Purchases.

You do not have to take this on faith. The game is readable source, with no minification and no bundled tracker, and it is public. Every line that touches a network lives in src/net/leaderboard.js and src/store/billing.js, and nothing else in the project makes a request of any kind.

What the game stores on your device

The save, one entry in your browser's localStorage, under the key little-rpg.save.v1. It holds your progress:

  • Stage, deepest stage, gold, kills
  • Upgrade levels, character level and experience
  • Talent, relic and soul trees, relics, souls, rebirths and awakenings
  • Soul dust, forged gear, dungeon keys, gems and your best gold rate
  • Gathering skills: levels, trees, tools, raw and refined resources
  • Pets: which are tamed, their levels, their armor and who is out on a trip
  • Potion and dish timers: seconds remaining on active effects
  • Lifetime counters used by feats and the bestiary: kills by species, bosses, deaths, forges, refines, feeds, brews, dungeon clears
  • Settings: buy-max, auto-forge, sound, music, damage numbers and language
  • The nickname you typed for the leaderboard, if you typed one, so it travels with an exported save
  • A timestamp of when you last had the game open, used only to work out offline earnings the next time you open it
  • If your copy sells gems: the store's receipt id for each gem pack already delivered, so an interrupted purchase is not paid out twice. The last fifty are kept

A device id, one entry under little-rpg.device.v1. It is a random UUID generated by your browser the first time the leaderboard needs one. It is not derived from your hardware, your account or anything about you, it is not an advertising identifier, and it exists for exactly one reason: so the board can tell that two submissions are the same player and keep one row instead of two. It is deliberately kept out of the save, so exporting your progress does not carry your board identity to another device.

Two leaderboard scratch entries, under little-rpg.lbqueue.v1 (one submission that failed to send, held until the next attempt) and little-rpg.lbcache.v1 (the last board you looked at, so it can be shown again without a round trip).

Clearing site data for wherever you play removes all of the above.

The game reads exactly two things from your browser beyond that: window.devicePixelRatio, so the pixel art renders sharply, and document.hidden, so the fight keeps running while the tab is in the background. Neither is stored and neither is sent. Sound is synthesized on your device as it plays; there are no audio files and nothing is recorded.

Export save shows you the exact data leaving with you: it is the save described above, encoded as one line of text, and it only goes where you paste it.

The leaderboard

The boards rank three leagues by deepest stage and by a weekly sprint. Taking part is what the following paragraphs describe.

What is sent. Six fields, and nothing else:

FieldWhat it is
device idthe random UUID described above
nicknamethe name you typed, or Hero if you never typed one
leaguewhich of the three leagues your spending puts you in
deepest stagethe highest stage this save has reached
weekly sprintyour best stage within the current week's window
week numberwhich week the sprint belongs to

When it is sent. Automatically, when you rebirth, when you awaken, when you open the boards, and when you save a nickname. It is not sent while you are simply playing, and it is never sent from a copy running on localhost.

Where it goes. To a database hosted by Supabase, run by us for this game alone. The submission is a single call that stores the best value it has seen for your device id; it cannot read anything else about you, because there is nothing else there. Rows are kept while the board is running. Supabase, and Vercel, which serves the game's files, will see the IP address your request arrives from, as any web host does, and each is an independent controller of its own server logs under its own policy.

What is public. Your nickname, your league and your stage numbers appear on a board other players can read. Your device id is never shown, and there is no way for another player to reach you.

Choose your nickname accordingly. It is free text that other people will see. Do not put your real name, your email, your school, or anything you would not paste into a public page.

How to be removed. Write to the address at the bottom of this page with the nickname you used, and we will delete the row. If you would rather not appear at all, do not save a nickname and do not rebirth while online, or play the downloaded single file, which never contacts anything.

The whole board is best-effort fun, not a record of anything. If the database ever goes away, the game keeps working exactly as it does now.

What the game does not do

  • No accounts, logins or profiles
  • No analytics, telemetry, crash reporting or usage statistics
  • No advertising, ad networks or advertising identifiers
  • No cookies
  • No third-party scripts, fonts, or content delivery networks. The game uses the monospace font already installed on your system
  • No chat, no messages, no way for one player to contact another
  • No selling or sharing of personal information with anyone
  • No requests of any kind beyond the leaderboard described above and a gem purchase you started. Switch the network off and the game still plays: it is installable and fully offline, and only the boards go quiet

Purchases

Little RPG is free to download and free to play. The only thing it ever sells is gems, and gems can also be earned by playing. Payment is handled entirely by the app store. We never see or receive your card number, billing address or payment credentials.

The pouch button at the top right opens the store. If your copy has a store attached, it lists gem packs with prices in your own currency; if it does not, it says so, and that copy sells nothing and makes no purchase of any kind. The version on the web has no store attached.

Where a store does exist, the purchase is carried out by the app store's own billing service. The game asks the store what the packs cost and tells it which one you chose; the store handles everything else.

What the game keeps afterwards is a purchase token for each pack it has credited, stored in your save. It is a pseudonymous receipt id issued by the store, and it exists so an interrupted purchase can be re-delivered without paying you twice. It contains no name, no email and no payment details.

A future version may send that token, with your device id and the pack id, to a small service of ours whose only job is to ask Google whether the purchase is genuine, so that a paying player is placed in the right league. It would learn nothing else, and this policy will say so plainly before that version ships.

The store is the party that collects and controls your purchase data. What it collects, how long it keeps it and what rights you have over it are governed by that store's privacy policy, not this one. Please read it.

What we receive from the store is limited to what it shows a developer: typically aggregate sales figures and payout records, and in some cases a pseudonymous purchase or refund identifier for support. We do not use any of it to build a profile.

If you contact us for support and include your email or an order number, we hold that message for as long as it takes to help you and no longer.

Where you got the game

This policy covers the game itself. It does not cover the platform you obtained it from or the connection you used to download it.

Any store or web host will see your IP address and request details simply because that is how the internet delivers a file, and stores additionally hold your account and purchase history. Those parties are independent controllers of that data under their own policies.

Your data, your control

  • Delete your progress from inside the game: Ascend tab, Awaken, then Erase everything and start over.
  • Delete everything from the browser: clear site data or local storage for wherever the game is running. This removes the save, the device id and the leaderboard scratch entries together.
  • Delete your leaderboard row: write to us with the nickname you used.
  • Back up or move your progress: the gear button at the top right, then Export save, which writes your whole save to a file; Import save reads it back anywhere. Your device id is not included, by design.

Saves are per-browser and per-origin. The downloaded single file opened from your disk and the hosted copy on the web keep separate saves, and clearing your browser data removes the save with it. We cannot recover a lost save, because we never had a copy, and that includes gems, whether they were cleared for or bought. Export is the only backup there is, and it is worth using before you clear browser data or change devices.

Children

The game has no chat, no messages and no advertising. It does have one piece of user-supplied text, the leaderboard nickname, which other players can see. A child should not use their real name for it, and the same warning is printed next to the field.

Purchases, where a store is attached, are made through that store, which applies its own age and parental controls.

Your rights

Privacy laws such as the GDPR (Europe), the LGPD (Brazil) and the CCPA (California) give you rights to access, correct, delete and port your personal data, and to object to its processing.

For your save, those rights are already in your hands: it is on your device, we never receive it, and you can export or erase it yourself at any time.

For the leaderboard, we hold one row: the fields listed above, keyed to a random device id. Write to the address below with the nickname you used and we will show you that row, correct it or delete it. Because the id is random and we hold nothing else, that nickname is the only way we can find it.

For purchase data, the store is the controller, and you exercise those rights with the store.

Changes to this policy

If the game starts collecting or transmitting anything beyond what is written here, this policy will be updated before that version ships. The date at the top always reflects the current version.
